Restoration ADDS a second route to No without resolving that: under a benefit-payability reading, restored 2.2 confines the Daily Hospital Income Benefit to hospitals in the United States and the query says 'traveling abroad'. But the query asks whether the policy will APPLY, and 4.1.1 insures You anywhere in the world, so on the applicability reading the timing question remains dispositive. Two independent contested routes now reach the same gold.

The operative insuring clause exists again: benefits are paid for confinement 'as a result of sickness or accidental Injury' (2.1), echoed by 2.2's 'due to sickness or accidental Injury'. A deliberate self-punch fails the trigger on the accidental-means reading, which is what the published gold needs. The accidental-results reading (the Landress v. Phoenix Mutual line) remains available, so the item stays interpretive - open texture in 'accidental' does not disappear - but the gold is now derivable from operative text instead of resting on a clause the benchmark's authors deleted.
